Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor

Class ToolbarButtonConfig

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.ToolbarButtonConfig
public final class ToolbarButtonConfig extends Object
The user's ordered toolbar button selection: which commands (extension toolbar contributions, and any future built-in id) appear in the editor's user-configured toolbar section, and how each is drawn. It is a plain, AWT-free value object so the whole model — ordering, add / remove / move, id validation and the '|'-joined persistence format — is testable headless, without a panel or a preference store.

Each ToolbarButtonConfig.Entry pairs a stable id (fully-qualified providerId/actionId for an extension contribution) with a ToolbarButtonConfig.DisplayMode that decides icon-only, text-only, or icon-and-text rendering. Entries are unique by id: adding an id already present just updates its mode rather than duplicating the button.

Validation is deliberately split: this class never drops an unknown id on load (a disabled extension must not corrupt the stored layout); the caller filters against the currently-available contributions at render time via resolve(Collection).

    • defaults

      public static ToolbarButtonConfig defaults()
      Returns:
      an empty configuration (the built-in toolbar buttons stand alone).

    • parse

      public static ToolbarButtonConfig parse(String text)
      Parses the '|'-joined id[:mode] persistence format written by toConfigString(). A blank / null string yields the empty (default) configuration; malformed entries (empty id) are skipped rather than throwing, so a corrupt store degrades gracefully.
      Parameters:
      text - the persisted string, may be null
      Returns:
      the parsed configuration, never null

    • toConfigString

      public String toConfigString()
      Returns:
      this configuration in the '|'-joined id:mode form, or "" when empty (so the caller can omit the preference entirely)

    • add

      public void add(String id)
      Appends id with the default mode, or updates its mode when already present (ids stay unique, no duplicate buttons). A blank id is ignored.
      Parameters:
      id - the stable contribution id

    • replaceFrom

      public void replaceFrom(Collection<ToolbarButtonConfig.Entry> newEntries)
      Replaces the whole ordered selection with newEntries (de-duplicated by id, preserving first-seen order). Used to load a working draft wholesale.
      Parameters:
      newEntries - the entries to adopt, may be null (clears)

    • move

      public boolean move(int index, int delta)
      Moves the entry at index by delta positions, clamped to the list ends (so "up" on the first and "down" on the last are no-ops).

      delta - the shift (-1 up / +1 down)
      Returns:
      true when a move actually happened
